source.title: On Large-Cohort Training for Federated Learning
source.authors: Zachary B. Charles; Zachary Garrett; Zhou-Yuan Huo; Sergei Shmulyian; Virginia Smith

record.tranche_reason: Tests the federated-learning analogue of cohort size as effective batch size, reporting train and test accuracy across cohort sizes. It is an extension to federated training rather than a centralized large-minibatch experiment.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own cohort-size results bearing on V5. It does not test the other versions. Figure-only accuracy values are not reconstructed; rows use the authors’ textual descriptions of those results.
record.test_reason: The study measures a federated analogue of large-batch training, rather than V5's batch-size effect under a fixed epoch budget. It varies clients per communication round while keeping client minibatch sizes fixed. At 1500 rounds, larger cohorts process more training examples and perform more aggregate local training. These results establish cohort-size effects but do not test the stated versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the extracted results: large cohorts can cause dataset- and optimizer-dependent generalization failures, and server learning-rate scaling has mixed efficacy. The paper additionally identifies diminishing returns, catastrophic training failures, fairness concerns, and reduced data efficiency, and offers partial remedies.
record.recipe_differences: Federated client-cohort size is varied across algorithms and datasets at a fixed 1500 communication rounds; this is not a centralized minibatch-size experiment at a fixed epoch budget.
record.method_sensitivity: The generalization effect varies by dataset and optimizer; square-root server learning-rate scaling has dataset- and cohort-size-dependent outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: At 1500 communication rounds, FedAdam on CIFAR-100 reaches similar training accuracy for cohorts of 50–400 clients while larger cohorts generalize worse. Cohort-related failures depend on dataset and optimizer and are absent on EMNIST and Stack Overflow.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing federated client cohort size at a fixed communication-round budget can reduce held-out accuracy despite similar training accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Square-root server learning-rate scaling with warmup improves CIFAR-100 accuracy, worsens Shakespeare test accuracy despite improved training accuracy, and has mixed effects on EMNIST and Stack Overflow.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Server learning-rate scaling with warmup has dataset- and cohort-dependent effects in federated learning.

record.problems: The main train/test accuracy comparisons are presented in figures, with precise values unavailable in the supplied text. The text gives an explicit same-training-accuracy comparison only for FedAdam on CIFAR-100; other dataset-level statements are less specific. The experiment uses federated cohorts and communication rounds rather than centralized minibatches and fixed epochs.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results were left out; figure results without sufficiently explicit text are not assigned reconstructed numerical values.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy in the same architectures and recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD training under the stated tuning conditions. Server-optimizer comparisons in federated local-SGD training do not isolate this benchmark claim.
Minibatch-size penalties under fixed epoch budgets and their recovery through longer training or adapted recipes. Client minibatch sizes remain fixed in the cohort sweeps.
Controlled effects of adding or removing dropout.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: States of cannot_determine refer to the stated claim versions, not uncertainty about the explicit cohort-size findings. No numerical plot values were inferred. The supplied text also contains inconsistent tuning descriptions: Section 2.1 specifies cohort size 50, whereas Appendix A.4 specifies 10.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image models.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization under the tuning conditions in the version.

Centralized minibatch size, fixed epoch budgets, and the version’s listed mitigations of longer training and normalization or regularization changes are not tested. The study varies federated client cohort size at 1500 communication rounds.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Varied federated cohort size and measured train and test accuracy after 1500 communication rounds using FedAdam.
rows.measure: Train and test accuracy; authors report roughly the same training accuracy across cohort sizes 50, 100, 200, and 400, with larger cohorts uniformly worse generalization.
rows.uncertainty: 5 random trials; one standard deviation shown in figures
rows.note: Textual description gives the comparison across the cohort-size sweep; precise plotted values are not stated in text.
rows.check: Cohort size 50 is the reference condition, not an independent observation of a large-batch penalty. The comparison concerns fixed communication rounds, not fixed epochs.

rows.operation_detail: Varied federated cohort size and measured train and test accuracy after 1500 communication rounds using FedAvg, FedAdam, and FedAdagrad.
rows.measure: Train and test accuracy; authors state generalization issues do not occur on EMNIST.
rows.uncertainty: 5 random trials; one standard deviation shown in figures

rows.check: The reported absence concerns cohort-related generalization failures, not large minibatches under a fixed epoch budget. Split the three optimizers into separate rows if retaining this result.

rows.check: The dataset-level statement does not establish each optimizer's outcome or justify partial. Cohort size at fixed rounds also does not measure V5.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Compared square-root server learning-rate scaling with no scaling, including warmup, in FedAvg after 1500 communication rounds.
rows.measure: Train and test accuracy; authors report improvement in both train and test accuracy for CIFAR-100.
rows.baseline: FedAvg with no scaling; figure only
rows.note: Numerical values are not stated in text.
rows.check: Improved accuracy from scaling the server learning rate measures a federated recipe effect. It does not establish recovery of a minibatch-size penalty under equal epoch budgets.

rows.subject: RNN with two LSTM layers
rows.operation_detail: Compared square-root server learning-rate scaling with no scaling, including warmup, in FedAvg after 1500 communication rounds.
rows.measure: Train and test accuracy; scaling improved training accuracy while reducing test accuracy.
rows.baseline: FedAvg with no scaling; figure only
rows.note: The text explicitly reports worse test accuracy despite improved training accuracy.
rows.check: Reduced test accuracy with server learning-rate scaling is explicit, but it does not reverse V5: the tested variable is a federated recipe at fixed rounds.

rows.note: The result varies with cohort size; exact values are figure-only.
